explicit_assumptions: DECK_ARCH is represented with both arch feet restrained in ux and uy and free in rz to expose a two-hinged-arch-like foundation-thrust path in the 2D F1 idealisation
THROUGH_ARCH and NETWORK_ARCH retain a left pin and right vertical roller because the DECK frame is the internal tie path
Signed axial diagnostic is (axial_j - axial_i) / 2, with positive tension and negative compression under the F1 local-force convention
A force is numerically detected only when its magnitude exceeds action_force_relative times the total applied force scale
A detected load path requires every ARCH_RIB element to remain in compression; a tied-arch path also requires every DECK element between the feet to remain in tension
For DECK_ARCH, the left horizontal support reaction must point right and the right reaction must point left
explicit_limitations: This study diagnoses an F1 linear load path; it performs no resistance, utilization, serviceability or code-compliance check
Both restrained DECK_ARCH feet are an idealised boundary condition and do not model abutment, bearing, foundation or soil stiffness
FRAME_2D joints remain rigid idealisations and TRUSS_2D hangers remain axial-only
No self-weight is generated; the parent user-supplied deck line load controls the study
No prestress, P-Delta, eigenvalue buckling, material nonlinearity, dynamic, wind, seismic, fatigue, connection or construction-stage analysis
FOUNDATION_THRUST_DETECTED and INTERNAL_TIE_ACTION_DETECTED mean only that the expected force path is numerically visible, not that any member or foundation is adequate
A source_ref, hash and clause_id establish provenance only; they do not prove engineering applicability
promotion_requirements: Independent review of support idealisation, reaction signs and element local-force convention
Cross-check foundation thrust and tie force against closed-form arch equilibrium and a separate trusted solver
Introduce bearing, abutment and soil/foundation stiffness with project-specific evidence
Add project load combinations, geometric nonlinearity, stability and section/foundation resistance checks before design use
